youtube.baslik: In sudden loss, why does the first audiogram record the time? #shorts
youtube.aciklama: When a person comes in with sudden hearing loss, the audiogram is recorded with date and time, because later follow-up measurements will be compared with this first value. Being fast does not mean measuring less: air and bone conduction are measured with the masking needed, and the speech recognition threshold and word recognition score are added when possible; an accurate first audiogram is the basis of every later comparison. The referral note first gives the date of onset and, if possible, the time; follow-up measurements use the same method, the same earphones and the same masking rules each time.
